ai.description: *Amolops himalayanus* is a medium-sized frog (45–60 mm) with a brown, mottled dorsum and pale venter. It features a distinct adhesive disc on each finger and a prominent, white supralabial stripe.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Amolops himalayanus* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, glandular dorsolateral fold and a prominent, broad adhesive disc on the tips of all fingers.
ai.habitat: *Amolops himalayanus* inhabits fast-flowing mountain streams within subtropical to temperate forests of the Himalayas, typically at elevations between 1,000 and 2,000 meters.
ai.behavior: *Amolops himalayanus* is primarily nocturnal, utilizing its specialized ventral sucker to cling firmly to slippery, moss-covered rocks within fast-flowing mountain streams.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Amolops himalayanus* breeds from May to July, laying small clutches of pigmented eggs attached to submerged rocks in fast-flowing Himalayan streams.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Amolops himalayanus* is found in the Eastern Himalayas across Arunachal Pradesh and West Bengal, typically inhabiting high-altitude streams between 1,000 and 2,500 meters.
ai.callDescription: The Himalayan Sucker Frog produces a series of short, high-pitched, whistled notes near fast-flowing mountain streams, where its calls cut through the sound of rushing water.
